items.label: Hendrickson-Ruiz theorem
items.thing: the Hendrickson-Ruiz theorem in topology
items.reply: The Hendrickson-Ruiz theorem states that for any connected graph $G$, its topological realization is embeddable in 3-space if and only if no minor of $G$ belongs to a specific obstruction set analogous to the Petersen family. In knot theory, it more broadly provides topological conditions for embedding spatial graphs such that their knotting and linking properties are fully determined by their planar components.
